property_summary: The owner() function must return the address that originally created the cooler (the first immutable arg), not the collateral address; the mutant makes it return the collateral address, breaking the invariant for all clones where owner and collateral differ.

For any clone, the `owner()` view must return the first immutable arg address (the original creator), not the collateral address; the mutant makes `owner()` equal to `collateral()`, violating the invariant when the two programmed addresses differ.

In the reference contract C, owner() must return the immutable creator address (first arg) and be distinct from collateral() whenever the two programmed addresses differ; the mutant makes owner() equal collateral(), so for any clone where creator and collateral differ, owner() != collateral() holds in the reference but fails in the mutant.

owner() must return the first immutable arg (creator) and NOT match collateral() when the two are different; the mutant sets owner() to collateral(), so for any clone where creator != collateral token, owner() equals collateral() in the bug but not in the reference.

For any clone, owner() must return the immutable creator address and must not equal collateral() whenever the two addresses are different; the bug makes owner() return collateral(), violating this inequality.

The owner() address read from the first 32 bytes of immutable args by reference is zero-padded on the left, while the buggy version reads the full 32-byte value and truncates from the left, so the returned address differs when any non-zero byte appears in the upper 12 bytes of that word.

Reading the owner() address from immutable args must return the address stored in the calldata at offset 0, right-shifted by 12 bytes; the bug reads the full 32-byte word without shifting, causing a mismatch whenever the upper 12 bytes of the immutable args word at offset 0 are non-zero.

The owner() address must be the 20-byte address stored right-padded in the first 32-byte immutable arg, but the buggy version returns the full 32-byte word truncated, which differs when any of the 12 upper bytes are non-zero.

Calling owner() must return address(uint160(uint256(calldataload(offset)) >> 0x60)), but the mutant returns address(uint160(calldataload(offset))), which differs whenever the upper 12 bytes of the first immutable-arg word are nonzero.
Owner() must return the address stored in the immutable args at offset 0, but the buggy version returns a different address when the upper 12 bytes of the first immutable arg word are non-zero.

The collateral() function returned by the reference contract correctly reads the collateral token address from immutable args at offset 0x14; the mutant returns a misaligned address from offset 0x15, violating the invariant that collateral() must equal the actual collateral token address passed during deployment.

The correct collateral() returns the address stored at immutable-args offset 0x14, so it must equal the collateral token set during clone deployment; the mutant at 0x15 returns a misaligned address, so they differ when the bytes at 0x14 and 0x15 are not identical.
